title: Finite congruence lattices: characterization and undecidability

issues.location: sections/weighted.tex, Thm t:weighted-realization / Thm t:weighted-product-success; sections/diophantine.tex Lemma n:circuit-template
issues.description: The undecidability proof needs an absolute stock integer S that is independent of the circuit. Its existence rests on the product-success and restart theorems, which state only that bounded marker losses exist and give no explicit value. The logic is sound, since the decider only needs S to exist and S can be hardwired. However, the uniformity claim (losses do not depend on the number of cohorts) is argued only briefly. I did not verify it line by line.
issues.evidence: "There are absolute initial cohort-stock and marker-loss bounds, independent of the numerical unit sizes and the number of cohorts"

coverage: Read and checked these parts line by line. (1) The graph criterion (Thm f:criterion) in both directions, and the Enumeration and bounds corollary. (2) The full Diophantine section: the positive-circuit reduction; the circuit-to-template encoding, including the factor-32 product identity (16(a+b))^2 = (16a)^2 + (16b)^2 + 512ab; the quantifier chain in Thm n:undecidable; and the subgroup-interval corollary. (3) The least-carrier argument in Prop f:prop-ordinary-interval: idempotent restriction, the nilpotent nonunit ideal, the join-preserving deflation Phi, and the diagonal construction [Delta(C) rtimes J, C^A rtimes J] with Lemma f:lem-subdirect. (4) Its weighted analogue, Prop t:weighted-algebra, which kills nilpotent deflations through atoms and parallel-line labels; also checked its top-order bound 60^m m!. (5) The template label structure (Lemma t:weighted-labels). (6) The four-block absorption test in Lemma t:weighted-normal-internal, including the bit equation s*eps + mu = (s+1)*eta. (7) Equal-totals reading (Prop t:weighted-equal-totals). (8) Primary-square reading (Thm t:weighted-square): the sign-graph argument showing L is even; the four-element base-kernel chain Delta S_x < A_x^x Delta S_x < (S_x^x)_even < S_x^x; the twin-class rank bound; binom(m',r) <= m'; and the odd count 2m'-3 for the near-complete case. (9) Compression lemma n:compression and the final template-count bound n:template-bound (complexity 24t, envelope formula). Only skimmed: the affine test-lattice construction and the CFSG, Larsen-Pink and highest-weight exclusions (sections classical, alternating, bounded, weights, reverse, marker_setup, forward_a, forward_b); weighted normal/product-success/restart/cuts/alignment (read the cuts and alignment proofs, not fully verified); counting rank-one and private-square propositions; the quantitative ceiling; and the Busy Beaver minimum section.
main_claim: A finite lattice is the full congruence lattice of a finite algebra exactly when it satisfies a finite colored-graph criterion. Deciding this representability from the lattice's order table is undecidable, so the finite lattice representation problem has a negative answer. A minimum nonrepresentable lattice (larger than 7 elements) has a finite Busy Beaver-based description, and recognizing full subgroup intervals [H,G] is also undecidable.
